What's confusing is that I don't see it on other geth nodes. ``` DEBUG[07-03|09:06:04.683] Message handling failed in `eth` id=e886365aa67a0db8 conn=dyndial err="invalid message: message msg #10 (787396 bytes): invalid message: (code a) (size 787396) rlp: expected input string or byte for *uint256.Int, decoding into (eth.PooledTransactionsPacket66).PooledTransactionsPacket[0](types.Transaction)(types.BlobTx).ChainID" ``` It could be that this is the first geth peer and it rejects it, but by that logic the sending node should have sent it to other peers too unrelated possibly, but nimbus was lagging for a bit and is now catching up and `b2df1473b8e3fbf9315236d1099bde516a3d002b` passes the hive tests (but this also has the selfdestruct EIP 6780, but on other 4844 features its essentially same the the commit the image is based off on, just few fixes to run hive tests) if i take a wild guess, is the encoding of new fields is 256 by geth's expectation? ahh i don't know the root cause, but i can see why nimbus is lagging: ``` DEBUG[07-03|09:18:36.059] Fetching batch of transactions id=0d9de040a6560389 conn=dyndial count=1 DEBUG[07-03|09:18:36.070] Message handling failed in `eth` id=0d9de040a6560389 conn=dyndial err="invalid message: message msg #10 (393774 bytes): invalid message: (code a) (size 393774) rlp: expected input string or byte for *uint256.Int, decoding into (eth.PooledTransactionsPacket66).PooledTransactionsPacket[0](types.Transaction)(types.BlobTx).ChainID" DEBUG[07-03|09:18:36.070] Removing Ethereum peer peer=0d9de040 snap=false ``` node peers with another, tries to fetch, fails since its invalid, disconnects peer and tries with another. keeps repeating in a loop i guess. but doesn't make sense that this one node has this problem also doesn't explain why nethermind-nimbus lags same issue i guess: ``` InMempoolForm trace at Nethermind.Serialization.Rlp.TxDecoder`1.EncodeTx(RlpStream stream, T item, RlpBehaviors rlpBehaviors, Boolean forSigning, Boolean isEip155Enabled, UInt64 chainId) ``` kinda confused why every node isn't failing :/ what did nimbus do specifically to trigger this in both geth/nethermind? Nimbus doesn't touch RLP (sort of, except if `--no-el` or a similar mode is used) yea, that'd what i'd expect as well the fcu nimbus sends should be ~same as what everyone else is doing FCUs also don't contain any RLP it should be a EL side issue, which is why its more confusing why it just happens on the 2 nimbus nodes :/ are those messages from devp2p gossip, or are those inputs somehow from Nimbus? I would assume its devp2p from the logs atleast `Message handling failed in eth id=0d9de040a6560389 conn=dyndial err...` it's odd because if Nimbus were screwing up the `newPayload` transfer, then it should be hitting other errors first (`INVALID_BLOCK` / `INVALID_BLOCK_HASH`, etc) Yeah, not that familiar with those logs in that level of detail, but looks like that to me Yeah and if it was a newPayload issue the node should forever be stuck on the same head, but it is moving forward (just slowly) sure, e.g., if it were some endianness issue hmm, i guess there's no easy way to do that without some geth console access? seeing some of these, shouldn't be happening either afaik: ``` DEBUG[07-03|09:49:12.127] Ethereum peer connected id=04b2fbf466631ed7 conn=dyndial name=Nethermind/v1.20.0-u... DEBUG[07-03|09:49:12.628] Fetching batch of transactions id=04b2fbf466631ed7 conn=dyndial count=20 DEBUG[07-03|09:49:12.879] Message handling failed in `eth` id=04b2fbf466631ed7 conn=dyndial err="message too long: 15091575 > 10485760" DEBUG[07-03|09:49:12.879] Removing Ethereum peer peer=04b2fbf4 snap=false DEBUG[07-03|09:49:17.296] Ethereum handshake failed id=a15d7f257651f59c conn=dyndial err=EOF DEBUG[07-03|09:49:19.315] Ethereum handshake failed id=0d36afe3be972980 conn=dyndial err=EOF INFO [07-03|09:49:24.079] Imported new potential chain segment number=20939 hash=9cd932..c8462b blocks=1 txs=0 mgas=0.000 elapsed="159.505µs" mgasps=0.000 dirty=86.14KiB ``` geth is peered to nethermind here, atleast according to the ID geth complaining about message too long would imply nethermind is sending a longer than expected message. Is the length not standard/not checked <@277500722655002624> ? It may mean we send like 18 transactions 6 blobs each But these transactions should be sent by request only def weird, will wait for marius to explain that then <@334704997122179072>, need your opinion We probably request transactions without a limit atm but then it fails at a downstream validation step? yep I've almost fixed the tx propagation issue thanks! wouldn't it be a dos vector if i can accept requests from peers wtihout a limit? i.e, couldn't nethermind be dossed if i request really large transaction counts We don't have 6780 enabled right? Can someone double check that this is a valid PooledTransactionETH66Packet Somehow our rlp decoding is beyond f'd like this? https://gist.github.com/miguelmota/9099b705cf433336036065ab748c8404 is this connected to Nimbus in any way, or? no Decodes ok, 1 tx x 6 blobs there Could you decode this as well? Error, seems like RLP list was expected, but got RLP string Yep okay my whole encoding and decoding is fucked it works with itself but not with other clients Could you point me to your decoding/encoding for blob txs network packets? isn't that a hive check though? It's so weird We decode the transactions we get via rpc correctly, but the network ones not Even though they use the same format Yep, but it's distributed across some files: get request id https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/master/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.Network/P2P/Subprotocols/Eth/V66/Messages/Eth66MessageSerializer.cs#L26 then https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/master/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.Network/P2P/Subprotocols/Eth/V62/Messages/TransactionsMessageSerializer.cs#L47 (which means txs are in InMempoolForm and wrapped in rlp) is there some reason why nethermind then has that error message with decoding? ``` InMempoolForm trace at Nethermind.Serialization.Rlp.TxDecoder`1.EncodeTx(RlpStream stream, T item, RlpBehaviors rlpBehaviors, Boolean forSigning, Boolean isEip155Enabled, UInt64 chainId) ``` ahh yes, correct It's just a stack trace log ahh, similar to the blob one then Wanted to log every place of mempool form of transaction usage* still missing an explanation as to why nimbus-nethermind is lagging in that case. with geth its clear-ish, assuming its related to the RLP issue. Let me check that pair, my first and totally unproven guess is that those are CL's p2p troubles on a small network Left side has tx's rlp as rlp string Right side has tx's rlp raw Raw rlp is for eth_sendrawtransaction only as far as I remember We have a limit on sending requested transactions (sending PooledTransactionsMessage). MaxPacketSize is 102400. The only exception is when single tx is larger - then we are sending 1 tx even if limit is exceeded https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/master/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.Network/P2P/Subprotocols/Eth/V65/Eth65ProtocolHandler.cs#L133-L154 But it says 15091575 which is 19 time more than max 6 blob tx it could be 1 really big blob right? but even then, its more than `102400` Any blob tx is more than 102400 🤔 But less then 15091575 for sure why are they both different? is left client A and right client B or are they just different blobs? Clients A and B have different encoding for tx pool messages <@360491619402776577> seen this already? I know Why is the transaction type not part of the network message? (according to spec) > tx_payload_body - is the TransactionPayloadBody of standard EIP-2718 blob transaction > TransactionPayloadBody: > > [chain_id, nonce, max_priority_fee_per_gas, max_fee_per_gas, gas_limit, to, value, data, access_list, max_fee_per_data_gas, blob_versioned_hashes, y_parity, r, s] But I guess you're also not doing that <@277500722655002624> ? Which part? Wrap tx as RLP string? Should be wrapped by nethermind too not put the tx type? Yep, it's always before transaction in any form, but not in its rlp
